claim: app.py creates the app, loads module constants with from_object, creates the SQLAlchemy handle, defines login_required and all handlers; models.py holds Post; main.js attaches the click handler; Procfile starts gunicorn
Diagram edges (browser to handlers, handlers to Post and database, click script GET to the delete route, Bootstrap CDN) match source
Authentication compares form fields to config constants and sets logged_in; login_required returns JSON 401; /add repeats the session test and aborts 401; no user table or roles
Home handler queries every Post and renders them or the empty-state message; public
/add accepts POST only, needs the session flag else 401, commits, flashes and redirects
/login shows the form on GET and checks username then password on POST with different error texts
/logout removes logged_in, flashes and redirects; GET with no session check
/delete/<int:post_id> needs a session, deletes by id and returns JSON status 1, or status 0 with the exception text
/search/ reads query, loads all entries and the template filters case-insensitively on title and text; public
A click on any .entry element GETs the delete route with the heading id, then reloads the page
limitation: element removal happens only when status is 1 (see 7.4)

claim: Verified by reading and by running: db = SQLAlchemy(app) (line 40) builds the engine from the URL at line 26 (default file named by DATABASE, line 22); the fixture sets SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI only at line 16 of the test file, after that; teardown runs db.drop_all() (line 21). Scratch-copy run (Flask 3.0.0, Flask-SQLAlchemy 3.1.1, DATABASE_URL unset): 6 passed, project/flaskr.db lost its post table (no tables left), test.db hash unchanged. With DATABASE_URL set to another SQLite file holding one row, the same run dropped that file's post table. With test.db removed, test_database fails (1 failed, 5 passed), so it passes only because the tracked test.db exists in the working directory. CI has no environment override and the tracked default database has 0 rows, so nothing is lost there
limitation: the Postgres case (DATABASE_URL pointing at Postgres) is Inferred; the same drop was observed only with a SQLite URL; runs were on a scratch copy in TEMP, never in the target
